extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: MATHVISTA is a consolidated benchmark designed to evaluate mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples combining challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA).
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. In International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2024). arXiv:2310.02255
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA and 19 VQA) and three newly curated datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). IQTest comprises 228 examples requiring inductive reasoning, abstract thinking, pattern prediction, and calculations, sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms. FunctionQA contains 400 examples emphasizing visual perceptions of functional plots and algebraic reasoning. PaperQA contains 107 examples featuring questions derived from academic illustrations (tables, figures, charts) sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Hugging Face.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets (Geometry3K, GeoQA+, GEOS, UniGeo, CLEVR-Math, IconQA, TabMWP, SciBench, TheoremQA, ChartQA, FigureQA, DVQA, MapQA, PlotQA, DocVQA, AI2D, ScienceQA, TQA, A-OKVQA, KVQA, ParsVQA-Caps, TextVQA, VizWiz, VQA2.0, PMC-VQA, VQA-RAD, Super-CLEVR, VQA-AS), puzzle test figures from online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic papers released in August 2023 on Hugging Face.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset was capped at up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. The full dataset of 6,141 examples was divided into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) using a two-step sampling strategy: first randomly sampling questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset, and then randomly sampling remaining questions based on their proportion in the entire set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic rules using a dictionary of quantity words and numeric answer filters were designed to automatically filter math-related candidates from over 70 general VQA datasets, yielding 4,949 candidate examples for human verification. Extracted answers were normalized to standard required answer formats (such as option letters, integers, floating-point numbers, or lists).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Candidate VQA examples were manually labeled by three expert annotators using majority voting to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning. For the three new datasets, all questions were manually authored and annotated by STEM graduate students through an independent two-step review process. Discrepancies were resolved via group discussion to reach consensus. Metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and mathematical reasoning skills were annotated.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom graphical user interface (GUI) annotation tools developed by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement for identifying mathematical reasoning among three annotators was measured using Fleiss Kappa, yielding a score of 0.775. For the newly collected datasets, independent annotations showed an inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2% (6 disagreements out of 736 questions resolved via consensus). For mathematical reasoning category labeling, automatic annotations showed 94.1% exact match and 98.79% individual label agreement compared to human expert annotations on 1,000 examples.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test set (5,141 examples) will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination; an online evaluation platform is maintained. The authors committed to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise based on community feedback, and updating the leaderboard with new models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to push general-purpose AI agents toward mastering visually rich and mathematically intensive tasks, supporting applications such as educational problem-solving, statistical data query assistance, theorem proving, and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage may have gaps in representing certain mathematical problems and visuals. High-quality data collection in specific scientific and college-level math domains is labor-intensive, posing challenges for scalability and generalizability. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations due to source heterogeneity, lacking a unified annotation format and structure across sources.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing, Validation, Benchmarking foundation models (LLMs and LMMs) on mathematical reasoning in visual contexts. Split into testmini (1,000 examples) for model development/validation and test (5,141 examples) for standard evaluation.
